answer: Vouching capacity follows the square root of standing. Each sponsor draws from a lagoon of standing earned one unit per graded epoch, and may vouch for at most that lagoon's square root in seats. A grove of ten aliases therefore needs one hundred units behind it, which is a hundred epochs of the sponsor's own graded work, while a single newcomer needs one. Standing cannot be borrowed, pooled or bought: only the sponsor's own record feeds the lagoon, and the cap binds on the sponsor alone. The oasis at the center is that record; the grove at the edge is what it can carry.
